paper.abstract_en: Graph theory is a powerful tool in quantum computing, with applications ranging from quantum circuit synthesis and optimization to entanglement mapping. Recent work has shown how one can use edge-colored graphs to model photonic experiments that generate GHZ and W states. However, the latter work also proved that verifying that a graph models a Dicke state experiment is coNP-complete. In this work, we provide families of graphs that generate $|D_{k}^a\rangle \otimes |0\rangle^{\otimes b }$, where $b = |a-2k|$ is the number of spectator modes. The graph setup consists of a doubled complete subgraph on $a$ vertices and a collection of auxiliary vertices. We prove that every coincidence carries exactly $k$ excitations, every weight-$k$ computational basis state on bitstrings of length $a$ is realized, and each of those bitstrings is realized exactly $(n/2)!$ times, where $n = a+b$. Since verifying the Dicke FORALL condition is coNP-complete in general, constructing explicit families that provably generate Dicke states is of interest.
